newsitem.title: USA: Zenith sees second-half '97 revenue growth.
newsitem.headline: Zenith sees second-half '97 revenue growth.

text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp said Tuesday it expects revenue growth for the second half of 1997 as it focuses on higher-margin home theater television systems and new "convergence" television products.
Convergence products include equipment that enables televisions to access the Internet and offer expanded interactive functions.
Zenith is also planning a multi-million-dollar national advertising campaign, its first in five years.

In addition, Zenith said it expects to begin shipping high-resolution computer display tubes to computer monitor manufacturers by mid-year. It also will begin initial shipments of new digital set-top boxes to telecommunications companies under a five-year, $1.0 billion contract with the Americast consortium that was signed last August.
A Zenith spokesman said the company is not issuing a projection for first half revenues.
Earlier, it reported revenues for 1996 of $1.29 billion, up from $1.27 billion in 1995.

Zenith said that, to support its 1997 business plan, it is seeking financing for planned capital investment projects and working capital requirements. A spokesman said these capital needs total in the "hundreds of millions" of dollars.

It added that existing credit agreements, amended at year-end 1996, continue in place as the company moves toward completing its new financing, which will be supported by its majority shareholder, LG Electronic Inc.
Zenith reported a loss for the fourth quarter of $1.05 a share after about $40.0 million in unusual charges, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.42.
For the year, it had a loss of $2.73 a share, which included about $80.0 million of unusual charges, compared with a loss of $1.85 in 1995.
Zenith said the charges taken in 1996 reflect aggressive actions to stabilize its cost structure and improve operating performance.
"We are confident that the actions we have taken position Zenith for major performance improvements in 1997 and beyond," Peter Willmott, president, said in a statement.
Zenith said it made net capital investments of about $125 million in 1996.

Operating results in 1996 were hurt by delays from production of higher-end consumer electronics products, particularly analog set-top boxes, and higher expenses related to the launch of digital products in 1997, Zenith said.
However, Zenith said it gained market share in its core domestic television business, with higher direct-view color television unit sales in a down industry.
